subject: Dedicated fleet sizing workbook and clarifying traffic samples
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@claritycommerce.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Fleet estimate request + workload sample

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this — we’re evaluating reserved GPU capacity for ClarityCommerce to support our new conversational commerce feature. I attached a small sample of our traffic telemetry (clarity_sample_workload.csv). High level:

- Current production footprint (beta): ~80 sustained concurrent sessions, primarily short chat flows.
- Daily burst pattern: three short windows where concurrency spikes to 600–750 for ~7–12 minutes each (peak day).
- Prompt/response mix: prompts average ~180 tokens, responses average ~420 tokens (median).
- Session behavior: around 60% single-turn completions, 40% multi-turn (avg 3 turns when multi-turn).
- KV cache: we perform prefix caching for repeated user queries; rough observed hit-rate ~25% on sample.
- Streaming: client streams tokens back to users in ~85% of responses.

What we would like from Redwood: a conservative dedicated fleet sizing recommendation for a pilot (predictable latency P95 <= 400ms for synchronous chat), an ops runbook for burst handling, and a rough monthly cost estimate for committed capacity (pilot: 3 months). Timeline: aiming to sign the pilot early January.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the CSV if helpful.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Product
ClarityCommerce

Attachment: clarity_sample_workload.csv (CSV, 38KB)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma@claritycommerce.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 17:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet estimate request + workload sample

Emma — thanks for the sample and the clear context. We can get a conservative pilot recommendation ready before the holidays. To make the sizing workbook specific to your workload I have a short intake checklist below — if you can share the highlighted items we’ll populate the workbook and run a cost/latency simulation. I attached a starter workbook (redwood_fleet-sizing-workbook.xlsx) that you can fill in.

Key items we need (short answers are fine):
1) Token distributions: exact histogram or percentiles for prompt tokens and response tokens (p50/p90/p99). If you only have averages, note that.
2) P95 latency SLO target for user-facing synchronous requests (you mentioned 400ms — confirm if soft/hard).
3) Concurrent session definition: do you count long-lived websocket sessions or per-request concurrency?
4) Burst windows: start/end times and recurrence (daily/weekly). For the spikes you reported, confirm if they are simultaneous geographically or spread across regions — affects routing.
5) Session duration and average number of tokens per session (aggregate of prompts+responses).
6) KV cache semantics: avg kvcache hit rate, typical prefix length, and whether cached responses are used for streaming.
7) Model behavior: whether you need sampling/temperature-based responses, function/tool calling frequency, or heavy decoding (long generation).
8) Throughput tolerance: acceptable queueing/backpressure (do you want to reject when overloaded, or queue for up to X seconds?).
9) Embeddings / vector workloads: frequency and whether they should share fleet or be routed separately.
10) Security: any private deployment/KMS requirements for the pilot.

A few notes up front based on the CSV: the burst shape looks very peaky (short but high concurrency). For that pattern we usually recommend mixing a reserved baseline capacity sized for sustained concurrency and a small burst pool that can be ephemeral (or routed to hosted fallback) to avoid large commits. The workbook will model: token throughput, batching gains, KV cache delta (we’ll run runs with hit-rate 0/25/50%), and two hardware profiles (A100-80GB vs 4xH100-80GB equiv).

Would you be available for a 30-min calibration call Monday (Dec 21) or Wed (Dec 23)?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_fleet-sizing-workbook.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Li <emma@claritycommerce.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet estimate request + workload sample

Looping in a few practical sizing assumptions from the infra side — I ran a quick pass on the CSV and sketched a baseline that we can refine once we have the percentiles. Quick takeaways: 

- Starting assumption: 80 sustained concurrency -> baseline fleet to meet p95=400ms with continuous batching is roughly 6–8 x A100-80GB equivalence when running a 13B-class instruct model with q4_0 quantization and modest KV cache usage.
- Burst headroom: to absorb 650–750 concurrency spikes without violating p95 we recommend either a) ephemeral burst pool (3–4 A100 equiv) + autoscale policy with warm-up, or b) routing excess to hosted standby model (cheaper but multi-tenant).
- Streaming cost/latency: streaming reduces perceived latency but prevents aggressive batching in the last-token window. For your 85% streaming usage we’ll model a 15–22% penalty on batching efficiency.
- KV cache impact: at 25% hit-rate we typically see 12–18% effective token reduction; this is significant for cost but less helpful for P95 during narrow bursts.

Questions I’ll use to tune the workbook: which model family are you evaluating for the feature (heavy instruction, long-form generation, or short chitchat)? Do you plan to quantize to int8/q4 or use FP16 for pilot? Also, confirm whether embeddings are batched independently — if so they should be on a separate pool.

I’ll drop a pre-populated workbook before our call with three scenarios (Conservative, Typical, Aggressive) and cost delta per month for each.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
